ei.title: The Science Behind the Mona Lisa
ei.subject: 영어1

fullPassage:
The Science Behind the Mona Lisa

Leonardo da Vinci is known as one of the most intelligent painters in the history of art. Although he is best known for his artistic masterpieces, he was also an accomplished scientist. During the Renaissance, art and science were not perceived as mutually exclusive. Rather, one was seen as informing upon the other. In fact, it was largely through a scientific approach to art that da Vinci created the outstanding masterpieces for which he is famous. One example is the Mona Lisa. This painting utilizes da Vinci's scientific knowledge as well as his magnificent artistic skills. Da Vinci was fascinated by how a smile begins to form. So, he evaluated every possible movement of each part of the face to determine the origin of nerves that control each facial muscle. This interest in anatomy allowed him to produce Mona Lisa's mysterious smile. He also carefully positioned the torso, head, and eyes so that each element is slightly turned, while the eyes still face the viewer. Hence, we have the perception that the eyes, which are staring straight out, are looking at us, even when we are not directly in front of the painting. Additionally, da Vinci created the illusion of depth in the painting. The farther the object is, the smaller the scale, the more subtle the colors, and the less detailed the outlines are.

questions.passage: Leonardo da Vinci is known as one of the most intelligent painters in the history of art. Although he is best ①<u>known</u> for his artistic masterpieces, he was also an accomplished scientist. During the Renaissance, art and science were not perceived as ②<u>mutual</u> exclusive. Rather, one was seen as ③<u>informing</u> upon the other. In fact, it was largely through a scientific approach to art that da Vinci ④<u>created</u> the outstanding masterpieces for which he is famous.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② mutual → mutually (부사가 형용사 exclusive 수식)
det.analysis:
✅ ①known: be known for(~으로 알려지다) 수동태 정상

❌ ②mutual → mutually: exclusive(형용사)를 수식하므로 부사 mutually가 필요. mutual(형용사)은 형용사 수식 불가 ←정답

✅ ③informing: be seen as informing(동명사 보어) 정상

✅ ④created: 과거시제 동사 정상
det.tip: 형용사를 수식하려면 부사 형태(mutually)를 써야 한다. mutual은 형용사라 exclusive를 수식할 수 없다.

questions.passage: Leonardo da Vinci is known as one of the most intelligent painters in the history of art. This painting utilizes da Vinci's scientific knowledge as well as his magnificent artistic skills. Da Vinci was fascinated by how a smile begins to form. So, he ①<u>evaluated</u> every possible movement of each part of the face to determine the origin of nerves ②<u>that</u> control each facial muscle. This interest in anatomy allowed ③<u>him</u> to produce Mona Lisa's mysterious smile. He also carefully positioned the torso, head, and eyes so that each element is slightly ④<u>turning</u>, while the eyes still face the viewer.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ turning → turned (수동태 be + p.p.)
det.analysis:
✅ ①evaluated: 과거시제 동사 정상

✅ ②that: 주격 관계대명사(선행사 nerves) 정상

✅ ③him: allow + 목적어(him) + to V 구조 정상

❌ ④turning → turned: 'each element is slightly turned' — 수동태(be + p.p.) 구조. turning(현재분사)은 '돌아가고 있는'이라는 진행 의미로 문맥 부적합 ←정답
det.tip: is turned: 수동태. 각 요소가 '돌려진(turned)' 상태. is turning은 능동 진행으로 의미가 달라짐.

questions.passage: Leonardo da Vinci is known as one of the most intelligent painters in the history of art. Although he is best known for his artistic masterpieces, he was also an accomplished scientist. In fact, it was largely through a scientific approach to art ①<u>that</u> da Vinci created the outstanding masterpieces for which he is famous. One example is the Mona Lisa. This painting utilizes da Vinci's scientific knowledge as well as his magnificent artistic skills. He also carefully positioned the torso, head, and eyes so that each element is slightly turned, ②<u>while</u> the eyes still face the viewer. Hence, we have the perception that the eyes, ③<u>which</u> are staring straight out, are looking at us, even when we are not directly in front of the painting. Additionally, da Vinci created the illusion of depth in the painting. The farther the object is, the ④<u>more smaller</u> the scale.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ more smaller → smaller (이중비교 오류)
det.analysis:
✅ ①that: It was ~ that 강조구문의 that 정상

✅ ②while: '~하는 반면에' 접속사 정상

✅ ③which: 계속적 용법 관계대명사(선행사 the eyes) 정상

❌ ④more smaller → smaller: smaller는 이미 비교급. more + 비교급은 이중비교로 문법 오류 ←정답
det.tip: the + 비교급, the + 비교급 구문: smaller가 이미 비교급이므로 more를 붙이면 이중비교 오류.

questions.passage: Leonardo da Vinci is known as one of the most intelligent painters in the history of art. Although he is best known for his artistic masterpieces, he was also an accomplished scientist. During the Renaissance, art and science were not perceived as mutually ①<u>exclusive</u>. Rather, one was seen as informing upon the other. In fact, it was largely through a scientific approach to art that da Vinci created the ②<u>outstanding</u> masterpieces for which he is famous. Da Vinci was fascinated by how a smile begins to form. So, he evaluated every possible movement of each part of the face to determine the origin of nerves that control each facial muscle. This interest in anatomy allowed him to produce Mona Lisa's ③<u>obvious</u> smile. He also carefully positioned the torso, head, and eyes so that each element is slightly turned, while the eyes still ④<u>face</u> the viewer.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ obvious(명백한) → mysterious(신비로운)
det.analysis:
✅ ①exclusive: mutually exclusive(상호 배타적인) — 원문 일치, 적절

✅ ②outstanding: outstanding masterpieces(뛰어난 걸작) — 원문 일치, 적절

❌ ③obvious → mysterious: 원문은 'Mona Lisa's mysterious smile'. obvious(명백한)는 모나리자 미소의 신비로움과 정반대 ←정답

✅ ④face: the eyes still face the viewer(눈이 관람자를 향하다) — 원문 일치, 적절
det.tip: 모나리자의 미소는 mysterious(신비로운)로 유명. obvious(명백한)는 반의어.

questions.passage: Leonardo da Vinci is known as one of the most intelligent painters in the history of art. Although he is best known for his artistic masterpieces, he was also an accomplished scientist. During the Renaissance, art and science were not perceived as mutually exclusive. In fact, it was largely through a scientific approach to art that da Vinci created the outstanding masterpieces for which he is famous. One example is the Mona Lisa. This painting utilizes da Vinci's scientific knowledge as well as his ①<u>magnificent</u> artistic skills. He also carefully positioned the torso, head, and eyes so that each element is slightly turned, while the eyes still face the viewer. Hence, we have the perception that the eyes, which are staring straight out, are looking at us, even when we are not directly in front of the painting. Additionally, da Vinci created the ②<u>illusion</u> of depth in the painting. The farther the object is, the smaller the scale, the more ③<u>vivid</u> the colors, and the less ④<u>detailed</u> the outlines are.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ vivid(선명한) → subtle(미묘한)
det.analysis:
✅ ①magnificent: magnificent artistic skills(뛰어난 예술적 기량) — 원문 일치, 적절

✅ ②illusion: the illusion of depth(깊이의 환각) — 원문 일치, 적절

❌ ③vivid → subtle: 원문은 'the more subtle the colors'. 멀어질수록 색이 미묘해진다(subtle). vivid(선명한)는 반대 의미 ←정답

✅ ④detailed: the less detailed the outlines(윤곽이 덜 세밀한) — 원문 일치, 적절
det.tip: 멀어질수록 색이 subtle(미묘)해지는 것이 원근법. vivid(선명한)는 반대 방향.

questions.passage: Leonardo da Vinci is known as one of the most intelligent painters in the history of art. Although he is best known for his artistic masterpieces, he was also an accomplished scientist. During the Renaissance, art and science were not perceived as ____________. Rather, one was seen as informing upon the other. In fact, it was largely through a scientific approach to art that da Vinci created the outstanding masterpieces for which he is famous.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 가장 적절한 표현은?

det.korean: 상호 배타적인 — 예술과 과학은 배타적이지 않았다
det.analysis:
✅ ①mutually exclusive(상호 배타적인): 원문 일치. '배타적이지 않았다'가 문맥(not perceived as ~) ←정답

❌ ②deeply connected(깊이 연결된): not perceived as deeply connected는 문맥 반대(오히려 연결됨)

❌ ③equally important(동등하게 중요한): 본문 맥락과 부합하지 않음

❌ ④practically identical(사실상 동일한): 예술과 과학이 동일하다는 내용 없음
det.tip: mutually exclusive = 상호 배타적인. not ~ mutually exclusive: 서로 배타적이지 않았다.

questions.passage: Da Vinci was fascinated by how a smile begins to form. So, he evaluated every possible movement of each part of the face to determine the origin of nerves that control each facial muscle. This interest in anatomy allowed him to produce Mona Lisa's mysterious smile. He also carefully positioned the torso, head, and eyes so that each element is slightly turned, while the eyes still face the viewer. Hence, we have the perception that the eyes, which are staring straight out, are looking at us, even when we are not directly ____________.
questions.stem: 빈칸에 들어갈 가장 적절한 표현은?

det.korean: 그림 바로 앞에 있지 않을 때에도
det.analysis:
❌ ①aware of the painting(그림을 인식하는): 문맥상 위치가 아닌 인식을 말하므로 부적합

❌ ②close to the artist(화가에게 가까운): 화가가 아닌 그림이 문맥의 대상

❌ ③interested in the subject(주제에 관심 있는): 관심이 아닌 물리적 위치가 핵심

✅ ④in front of the painting(그림 앞에): 원문 일치. 그림 앞에 있지 않아도 눈이 우리를 보는 것 같다 ←정답
det.tip: in front of = ~앞에. 그림 정면에 있지 않아도 눈이 따라오는 효과.

questions.passage: Leonardo da Vinci is known as one of the most intelligent painters in the history of art. Although he is best known for his artistic masterpieces, he was also an accomplished scientist. During the Renaissance, art and science were not perceived as mutually exclusive. Rather, one was seen as informing upon the other. In fact, it was largely through a scientific approach to art that da Vinci created the outstanding masterpieces for which he is famous. One example is the Mona Lisa.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: Da Vinci was known primarily as a scientist, not a painter.
During the Renaissance, art and science were seen as completely separate.
Da Vinci used a scientific approach to create his famous masterpieces.
The Mona Lisa is the only masterpiece da Vinci ever created.

det.korean: 다빈치는 과학적 접근을 통해 유명한 걸작을 만들었다.
det.analysis:
❌ ①Da Vinci was known primarily as a scientist, not a painter(다빈치는 주로 과학자로 알려졌다): 본문은 'best known for his artistic masterpieces'로 화가가 우선

❌ ②art and science were seen as completely separate(예술과 과학이 완전히 분리된 것으로 보였다): 본문은 'not perceived as mutually exclusive'로 정반대

✅ ③Da Vinci used a scientific approach to create his famous masterpieces(다빈치는 과학적 접근을 사용하여 유명한 걸작을 만들었다): 'through a scientific approach to art that da Vinci created' 일치 ←정답

❌ ④The Mona Lisa is the only masterpiece(모나리자가 유일한 걸작): 'One example is the Mona Lisa'로 하나의 예시일 뿐
det.tip: through a scientific approach to art = 예술에 대한 과학적 접근을 통해.

questions.passage: Leonardo da Vinci is known as one of the most intelligent painters in the history of art. Although he is best known for his artistic masterpieces, he was also an accomplished scientist. During the Renaissance, art and science were not perceived as mutually exclusive. Rather, one was seen as informing upon the other. In fact, it was largely through a scientific approach to art that da Vinci created the outstanding masterpieces for which he is famous. One example is the Mona Lisa. This painting utilizes da Vinci's scientific knowledge as well as his magnificent artistic skills. Da Vinci was fascinated by how a smile begins to form. So, he evaluated every possible movement of each part of the face to determine the origin of nerves that control each facial muscle. This interest in anatomy allowed him to produce Mona Lisa's mysterious smile.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: Da Vinci studied facial muscles to understand how a smile forms.
Da Vinci's knowledge of anatomy had no influence on the Mona Lisa.
Da Vinci examined every possible movement of each part of the face.
The Mona Lisa combines scientific knowledge and artistic skills.

det.korean: 다빈치의 해부학 지식이 모나리자에 영향을 미치지 않았다는 것은 사실이 아니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ①Da Vinci studied facial muscles to understand how a smile forms(다빈치가 미소가 형성되는 방식을 이해하기 위해 안면 근육을 연구했다): 'evaluated every possible movement... to determine the origin of nerves' 일치

❌ ②Da Vinci's knowledge of anatomy had no influence on the Mona Lisa(다빈치의 해부학 지식이 모나리자에 영향이 없었다): 'This interest in anatomy allowed him to produce Mona Lisa's mysterious smile'과 정반대 ←정답

✅ ③Da Vinci examined every possible movement(모든 가능한 움직임을 평가했다): 원문과 일치

✅ ④The Mona Lisa combines scientific knowledge and artistic skills(모나리자는 과학적 지식과 예술적 기술을 결합한다): 'utilizes da Vinci's scientific knowledge as well as his magnificent artistic skills' 일치
det.tip: 본문: 'This interest in anatomy allowed him to produce Mona Lisa's mysterious smile.' 해부학이 모나리자에 직접 기여.

questions.passage: He also carefully positioned the torso, head, and eyes so that each element is slightly turned, while the eyes still face the viewer. Hence, we have the perception that the eyes, which are staring straight out, are looking at us, even when we are not directly in front of the painting. Additionally, da Vinci created the illusion of depth in the painting. The farther the object is, the smaller the scale, the more subtle the colors, and the less detailed the outlines are.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: The eyes of the Mona Lisa appear to follow the viewer regardless of position.
The torso, head, and eyes of the Mona Lisa all face the same direction.
Objects farther away in the painting have more vivid colors.
The outlines in the painting become more detailed as objects recede.

det.korean: 모나리자의 눈은 위치에 관계없이 관람자를 따라가는 것처럼 보인다.
det.analysis:
✅ ①The eyes appear to follow the viewer regardless of position(눈이 위치에 관계없이 관람자를 따라간다): 'looking at us, even when we are not directly in front of the painting' 일치 ←정답

❌ ②torso, head, and eyes all face the same direction(몸통, 머리, 눈이 모두 같은 방향): 'each element is slightly turned' — 살짝 돌아가 있음, 같은 방향 아님

❌ ③Objects farther away have more vivid colors(멀리 있는 물체가 더 선명한 색): 'the more subtle the colors' — 더 미묘해짐

❌ ④outlines become more detailed as objects recede(물체가 멀어질수록 윤곽이 더 세밀해짐): 'the less detailed the outlines' — 덜 세밀해짐
det.tip: even when we are not directly in front = 정면에 있지 않아도. 눈이 따라오는 효과.

questions.passage: Leonardo da Vinci is known as one of the most intelligent painters in the history of art. Although he is best known for his artistic masterpieces, he was also an accomplished scientist. During the Renaissance, art and science were not perceived as mutually exclusive. Rather, one was seen as informing upon the other. In fact, it was largely through a scientific approach to art that da Vinci created the outstanding masterpieces for which he is famous. This interest in anatomy allowed him to produce Mona Lisa's mysterious smile.
questions.stem: 이 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: the biography of Leonardo da Vinci as a Renaissance artist
the historical importance of the Mona Lisa in European culture
the difference between Renaissance art and modern art techniques
how da Vinci's scientific knowledge contributed to his masterpieces

det.korean: 다빈치의 과학적 지식이 그의 걸작에 어떻게 기여했는가
det.analysis:
❌ ①the biography of Leonardo da Vinci(레오나르도 다빈치의 전기): 전기가 아니라 과학과 예술의 융합이 주제

❌ ②the historical importance of the Mona Lisa in European culture(유럽 문화에서 모나리자의 역사적 중요성): 역사적 중요성이 아닌 과학적 기법이 핵심

❌ ③the difference between Renaissance art and modern art(르네상스와 현대 미술의 차이): 현대 미술 비교는 본문에 없음

✅ ④how da Vinci's scientific knowledge contributed to his masterpieces(다빈치의 과학적 지식이 걸작에 어떻게 기여했는가): 본문 전체 주제 ←정답
det.tip: 본문 핵심: through a scientific approach to art + interest in anatomy + illusion of depth.

questions.passage: Leonardo da Vinci is known as one of the most intelligent painters in the history of art. Although he is best known for his artistic masterpieces, he was also an accomplished scientist. During the Renaissance, art and science were not perceived as mutually exclusive. So, he evaluated every possible movement of each part of the face to determine the origin of nerves that control each facial muscle. questions.stem: 이 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: All great Renaissance painters were trained scientists before becoming artists.
The Mona Lisa became famous solely because of its realistic depiction of depth.
Da Vinci's integration of scientific inquiry and artistic skill produced his iconic works.
Understanding anatomy is the only requirement for creating great paintings.

det.korean: 다빈치의 과학적 탐구와 예술적 기량의 통합이 그의 상징적 작품을 만들어냈다.
det.analysis:
❌ ①All great Renaissance painters were trained scientists(모든 르네상스 화가가 과학자였다): 다빈치에 한정된 내용이며 모든 화가를 일반화하지 않음

❌ ②The Mona Lisa became famous solely because of depth(모나리자가 오직 깊이 묘사 때문에 유명해졌다): 미소, 눈의 배치 등 여러 요소가 언급됨. solely는 과장

✅ ③Da Vinci's integration of scientific inquiry and artistic skill produced his iconic works(과학적 탐구와 예술적 기량의 통합이 상징적 작품을 만들어냈다): 본문 전체 요지 ←정답

❌ ④Understanding anatomy is the only requirement(해부학 이해가 유일한 요건): only는 과장. 깊이의 환각, 배치 등 다른 요소도 언급
det.tip: 요지: 과학적 접근(해부학+원근법) + 예술적 기량 = 걸작.

questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 This interest in anatomy allowed him to produce Mona Lisa's mysterious smile이 함축하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: Da Vinci preferred studying medicine over creating art.
Scientific understanding of the human body directly enhanced artistic expression.
The mysterious smile was an accidental result of anatomical studies.
Anatomy lessons were mandatory for all painters during the Renaissance.

overlay.underline: This interest in anatomy allowed him to produce Mona Lisa's mysterious smile

det.korean: 인체에 대한 과학적 이해가 예술적 표현을 직접적으로 향상시켰다.
det.analysis:
❌ ①Da Vinci preferred studying medicine over creating art(다빈치가 예술보다 의학을 선호했다): 의학 선호가 아닌 예술에 과학을 활용한 것

✅ ②Scientific understanding of the human body directly enhanced artistic expression(인체에 대한 과학적 이해가 예술적 표현을 직접 향상시켰다): 해부학(anatomy) 지식이 신비로운 미소 창작을 가능하게 했다는 함축 ←정답

❌ ③The mysterious smile was an accidental result(신비로운 미소가 우연한 결과였다): 의도적 연구 결과이므로 우연이 아님

❌ ④Anatomy lessons were mandatory for all painters(해부학 수업이 모든 화가에게 의무였다): 모든 화가에 대한 일반화 없음
det.tip: interest in anatomy → allowed him to produce: 해부학 관심이 미소 창작을 가능하게 했다 = 과학이 예술을 향상시킴.

questions.passage: Leonardo da Vinci is known as one of the most intelligent painters in the history of art. Although he is best known for his artistic masterpieces, he was also an accomplished scientist. During the Renaissance, art and science were not perceived as mutually exclusive. Rather, <u>one</u> was seen as informing upon the other. In fact, it was largely through a scientific approach to art that da Vinci created the outstanding masterpieces for which he is famous.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 one이 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: one = 예술 또는 과학 중 하나
det.analysis:
✅ ①예술 또는 과학 중 하나: 'art and science... one was seen as informing upon the other' — one과 the other가 art/science를 대체 ←정답

❌ ②레오나르도 다빈치: 다빈치는 he로 지칭됨

❌ ③르네상스 시대: 시대를 one으로 지칭하지 않음

❌ ④모나리자 그림: 이 시점에서 아직 모나리자가 언급되지 않음
det.tip: one ~ the other: 둘 중 하나 ~ 나머지 하나. art와 science를 가리킴.

questions.passage: Da Vinci was fascinated by how a smile begins to form. So, he evaluated every possible movement of each part of the face to determine the origin of nerves that control each facial muscle. This interest in anatomy allowed him to produce Mona Lisa's mysterious smile. He also carefully positioned the torso, head, and eyes so that each element is slightly turned, while the eyes still face the viewer. Hence, we have the perception that the eyes, which are staring straight out, are looking at us, even when <u>we</u> are not directly in front of the painting.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 we가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: we = 그림을 보는 관람자들
det.analysis:
❌ ①다빈치와 그의 조수들: 다빈치는 he로 지칭, we는 일반적 관람자

❌ ②르네상스 시대의 과학자들: 특정 집단이 아닌 일반적 관람자

✅ ③그림을 보는 관람자들: 'are looking at us, even when we are not directly in front of the painting' — we = 그림을 보는 사람들 ←정답

❌ ④모나리자 작품의 소유자들: 소유자가 아닌 일반 관람자
det.tip: we are not directly in front of the painting: 그림 앞에 있는 we = 관람자.

det.analysis:

det.korean: 얼굴의 각 부분의 모든 가능한 움직임을 평가했다.
det.analysis:
✅ 'he evaluated every possible movement of each part of the face' — 미소가 형성되는 방식을 이해하기 위해 다빈치가 평가한 대상.

every possible movement(모든 가능한 움직임) + of each part of the face(얼굴의 각 부분의).
det.tip: evaluate: 평가하다. every possible: 모든 가능한. each part: 각 부분.

questions.passage: Leonardo da Vinci is known as one of the most intelligent painters in the history of art. Although he is best known for his artistic masterpieces, he was also an accomplished scientist. During the Renaissance, art and science were not perceived as mutually exclusive. Rather, one was seen as informing upon the other. In fact, it was largely through a scientific approach to art that da Vinci created the outstanding masterpieces for which he is famous. One example is the Mona Lisa. This painting utilizes da Vinci's scientific knowledge as well as his magnificent artistic skills. Da Vinci was fascinated by how a smile begins to form. So, he evaluated every possible movement of each part of the face to determine the origin of nerves that control each facial muscle. This interest in anatomy allowed him to produce Mona Lisa's mysterious smile. He also carefully positioned the torso, head, and eyes so that each element is slightly turned, while the eyes still face the viewer. Hence, we have the perception that the eyes, which are staring straight out, are looking at us, even when we are not directly in front of the painting. Additionally, da Vinci created the illusion of depth in the painting. The farther the object is, the smaller the scale, the more subtle the colors, and the less detailed the outlines are.
questions.stem:
위 글의 내용을 바탕으로 다음 질문에 대한 답을 본문에서 찾아 영어로 쓰시오. (10단어)

Q: What did da Vinci create in addition to the mysterious smile?
→ _______ _______ _______ _______ _______ _______ _______ _______ _______ _______.
questions.wa: da Vinci created the illusion of depth in the painting
accept: da Vinci created the illusion of depth in the painting
the illusion of depth in the painting

det.korean: 다빈치는 그림에서 깊이의 환각을 만들어냈다.
det.analysis:
✅ 'da Vinci created the illusion of depth in the painting' — 본문 마지막 부분에서 다빈치가 신비로운 미소 외에 추가로 만들어낸 것.

the illusion of depth(깊이의 환각/착시) + in the painting(그림에서). 원근법 기법.
det.tip: illusion: 환각, 착시. depth: 깊이. 원근법을 통해 2차원 그림에 3차원 깊이감을 만들어냄.

questions.ans: da Vinci created the illusion of depth in the painting

questions.passage: Leonardo da Vinci is known as one of the most intelligent painters in the history of art. Although he is best known for his artistic masterpieces, he was also an accomplished scientist. During the Renaissance, __________. Rather, one was seen as informing upon the other.

"예술과 과학은 상호 배타적인 것으로 인식되지 않았다"

[조건] (1) and, art, as, exclusive, mutually, not, perceived, science, were를 모두 사용할 것 (2) 9단어로 쓸 것 (9단어) (영어로)
questions.wa: art and science were not perceived as mutually exclusive
accept: art and science were not perceived as mutually exclusive

overlay.blank: art and science were not perceived as mutually exclusive

det.korean: 예술과 과학은 상호 배타적인 것으로 인식되지 않았다.
det.analysis: ✅ art and science(예술과 과학) + were not perceived(인식되지 않았다) + as mutually exclusive(상호 배타적인 것으로). 수동태 + as 보어 구조. 9단어 일치.
det.tip: be perceived as: ~으로 인식되다. mutually exclusive: 상호 배타적인.
